name: Ukraine: Russian invasion
summary: Russia seized Crimea and parts of the Donbas in 2014 and launched a full-scale invasion in February 2022. The war became the largest in Europe since 1945, with attritional ground fighting across the east and south and long-range strike campaigns by both sides.

peace.summary: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner met President Putin in Moscow to discuss a Ukraine settlement after the Abu Dhabi round; a meeting with Zelensky was also expected.
US, Russian and Ukrainian delegations held two days of talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November, focused on territory and security guarantees, and ended without a major breakthrough.
US envoy Steve Witkoff announced that the US would mediate trilateral talks between US, Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November, restarting talks suspended since February.

US envoys Witkoff and Kushner met Ukrainian, E3, European Commission and NATO officials in Miami. They discussed de-escalation before winter, energy security, grain exports and security guarantees ahead of the next US contact with Russia.

An energy ceasefire announced by President Trump in mid-October reportedly lasted only a few hours before Russia resumed strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, and Ukraine answered with mass drone attacks on 18 October.
A US-led trilateral round in January 2026 ended without agreement; Washington proposed a new round for late October 2026.

peace.summary: Trump–Putin summit in Anchorage produced no ceasefire; follow-up talks with Ukraine and European leaders in Washington on 18 August.
First direct Russia–Ukraine talks since 2022, in Istanbul, agreed prisoner exchanges but no ceasefire.
Istanbul talks on a draft neutrality treaty broke down in April 2022 as fighting continued.

history.status: US-mediated trilateral talks between the US, Russia and Ukraine resumed in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November 2026, the first round in nine months, but produced no breakthrough. US envoys Witkoff and Kushner then met Putin in Moscow on 12 November. Fighting continued: ISW reported Russian advances near Kupyansk, Lyman and Dobropillia on 21 November. Russian strikes on 22 November killed at least 15 people and hit energy sites, and on 23 November Ukraine said it had struck Russian ships off Libya.

On 9 October 2026 US envoys Witkoff and Kushner met Ukrainian, E3, EU and NATO officials in Miami to prepare for the next US contact with Russia. A US-announced energy ceasefire then collapsed within hours as Russian strikes on Ukraine's power grid continued. ISW reported Ukrainian counterattacks east of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, and on 18 October Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia, hitting St Petersburg oil terminals.

US-led talks stalled after a trilateral round in January 2026; Washington proposed a new round for late October.

name: Sudan: civil war
summary: A power struggle between the army and the paramilitary RSF erupted into open war in Khartoum in April 2023. It has produced the world’s largest displacement crisis, famine conditions, and mass atrocities in Darfur.

peace.summary: Nearly two dozen countries met in Geneva for UN-backed talks on a pathway to a ceasefire in Sudan and a transition to inclusive civilian rule. The army and the RSF did not agree to anything directly.
Army chief al-Burhan rejected talks and vowed to retake all RSF-held territory.

In early and mid-November the army and allied forces went on the offensive in North and West Kordofan, and Al Jazeera reported on 14 November that the RSF siege of El Obeid had been broken. The army carried out airstrikes on Nyala on 19 November. RSF drone strikes killed civilians in El Obeid and, on 22 November, in Khartoum, where a UN building was also damaged. Fighting also spread in Blue Nile.

Al Jazeera reported on 17 October that the army said it killed dozens of RSF fighters in an attack in Nyala. Army air and drone strikes killed civilians in North and West Kordofan on 15 and 17 October. On 19 October, RSF drones were shot down near Khartoum airport (three children were reported killed), and the army said it repelled an RSF–SPLM-N assault near Kurmuk in Blue Nile.

Fighting shifted to Kordofan in 2026: the RSF besieged El Obeid from mid-year while the army advanced on RSF positions, taking al-Mazroub in October 2026. The RSF and SPLM-N entered Kurmuk in Blue Nile in August 2026. Army chief al-Burhan rejected a US 90-day ceasefire plan put forward in September and in October 2026 vowed to retake all RSF-held territory; the RSF still holds almost all of Darfur.

name: Gaza: Israel–Hamas war
summary: Hamas’s 7 October 2023 attack killed about 1,200 people in Israel and took some 250 hostages. Israel’s ensuing campaign devastated Gaza, killing tens of thousands and displacing most of the population, and triggered a wider regional confrontation.

The Board of Peace told the UN Security Council that Israel and Hamas had failed to meet key ceasefire commitments and warned that the truce could collapse without immediate action.

Israeli media reported that Israel's government approved an initial deployment of about 250 foreign troops for the International Stabilization Force, with US military preparations underway near the Gaza border.

Board of Peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov demanded that Israel immediately let the International Stabilization Force and the Palestinian technocratic committee into Gaza, after Israel blocked construction of the force's base.
Netanyahu rejected the Board of Peace disarmament roadmap, demanding full disarmament before withdrawal.

history.status: Israeli strikes kept killing Palestinians in Gaza after 19 October 2026. On 12 November an airstrike on Khan Younis's Nasser Hospital killed six people, and on 23 November strikes killed at least three, including an UNRWA worker. Palestinian and Israeli tallies put the dead since the October 2025 truce at more than 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers. On 17 November the Board of Peace told the UN Security Council that the ceasefire could collapse because neither Israel nor Hamas had met key commitments.

The October 2025 ceasefire reached its first anniversary on 10 October 2026. More than 100 aid groups said it existed "in name only", and Gaza's Health Ministry reported 1,488 people killed between the start of the truce and 11 October. Israeli strikes killed more people on 14–15 October. Israel has still not let in contractors to build the base for the International Stabilization Force, and on 18 October Board of Peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov demanded that Israel let the force and the technocratic committee into Gaza.

name: Lebanon: Israel–Hezbollah war
summary: Hezbollah opened a front in support of Hamas in October 2023. Israel escalated in September 2024 with pager attacks, the killing of Hassan Nasrallah and a ground incursion into southern Lebanon.

peace.summary: Israeli and Lebanese military delegations held two days of US-mediated technical talks at CENTCOM in Tampa. Lebanon sought an end to escalation and an Israeli withdrawal; Israel pressed for a direct joint operations room.

Israel and Lebanon were set to hold US-hosted military talks at CENTCOM in Tampa on pilot zones, Lebanese army deployment and Israeli withdrawal; Lebanon said it would reject direct military coordination.

Lebanon pressed for an end to escalation and an Israeli withdrawal, while Israel pushed for a direct joint operations room. Violence has been sporadic but continues: a drone strike in Marjayoun district in early November killed one person, which Arab News reported as the first such death since September. On 16 November, Israel struck what it said was a Hezbollah arms shipment near the Syrian border. It hit a weapons site in eastern Lebanon on 19–20 November and demolished homes in the south on 18 November.

Israeli strikes in the south continued near-daily into October 2026.

name: Iran: US–Israel war
summary: Decades of shadow war became direct exchanges of fire in 2024 and a twelve-day Israeli air campaign in June 2025. On 28 February 2026 the United States and Israel launched a full-scale war on Iran, striking its leadership, nuclear and military sites; Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz and fired on Gulf states hosting US forces.

Qatar said it was still facilitating US–Iran negotiations, and Araghchi reportedly urged Iran's security leadership to advance the latest Qatari peace proposal.

Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran was still reviewing US comments, received through intermediaries, on its September seven-day ceasefire proposal, and that its conditions for reopening Hormuz still stood.

On 18 November Min Aung Hlaing announced a peace conference for February 2027, and on 19 November the ICJ ruled that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The AA has driven them back and damaged several navy vessels. Air strikes went on across the country, including about 30 in Sagaing and others in Mon and Magway. Fighting stayed intense, above all in Rakhine, where the Arakan Army holds most of the state and junta offensives on Sittwe and Kyaukphyu stalled in September 2026. history.status: On 12 November 2026, Pashinyan and Aliyev met at the European Political Community summit in Dublin and discussed the TRIPP route, trade, border delimitation and water cooperation. On 23 November Armenia published a draft constitution. Its preamble does not mention Nagorno-Karabakh or the Declaration of Independence. Azerbaijan's foreign minister Bayramov said the text appeared to contain no territorial claims and that Baku then sees no further obstacle to signing. The pro-Russian opposition rejects the draft. That pushes the signing well beyond earlier expectations. Baku still requires Armenia to change its constitution first. On 14 October his office denied reports that he had met Presidents Putin and Aliyev in Turkmenistan. No deadly border clashes were reported, and work on the TRIPP corridor is still being prepared.

Media reported that troops captured separatist commander 'General' Shaggy alive in Ekona (Southwest) on 16 October. history.status: Attacks on shipping rose sharply in October 2026. Ships were hit almost every day, at least 12 vessels were attacked in the week to 16 October, and strikes spread outside the strait. The IRGC formally declared the Strait of Hormuz closed on 17 October, US aircraft disabled a ship running the blockade on 10 October, and on 19 October the IRGC said a tanker using an 'unauthorized' route hit a mine and caught fire. On 18 October Iran said it was still reviewing US comments on its seven-day ceasefire and reopening plan.
